title: Programmers, executives and letter-writers
lede: Titles are as given in the press at the time. We have left out later careers where we have no source.

people.name: Jennifer Dorian
people.text: Presented the service at launch and gave its commercial case: a niche that was underserved, aimed at 25-to-44-year-olds who already paid for other services.[^4][^5]

people.name: Coleman Breland
people.role: President, Turner Classic Movies and FilmStruck
people.text: Called the service Turner’s “strategic move into the direct-to-consumer business” in 2016 and oversaw it to the end. Said in February 2018 that Turner had never thought about raising the price.[^1][^12][^19]

people.name: Peter Becker
people.text: Called FilmStruck “an arthouse film lovers’ dream streaming service” in the 2016 announcement and brought Criterion’s library over from Hulu.[^1][^3]
people.later: Criterion relaunched the Criterion Channel on its own in April 2019.[^35][^36]

people.name: John Martin
people.text: Announced FilmStruck as “a terrific example of our strategy to meet consumer demand for great content across all screens.”[^1]

people.name: Craig Hunegs
people.text: Closed Warner Archive’s streaming service into FilmStruck in February 2018, calling it “a pretty easy decision.” His division also ran DramaFever.[^12][^18]

people.name: Aksel van der Wal
people.role: Executive vice president, Turner International Digital Ventures & Innovation
people.text: Led the international roll-out to Britain, France and Spain.[^10][^14]

people.name: Kerensa Samanidis
people.text: A former British Film Institute executive appointed to run the service outside the United States.[^14][^19]

people.name: Ben Mankiewicz
people.text: Recorded introductions for TCM Select, the monthly collection of Warner Bros. classics added in February 2018.[^12]

people.name: John Stankey
people.text: The AT&T executive who announced the company’s large streaming service in October 2018. Spielberg and Scorsese took their appeal to him, and Deadline reported that he was working on a compromise.[^22][^28][^32]

people.name: Toby Emmerich
people.text: The addressee of the filmmakers’ letter, though FilmStruck was not his to run. A source told The Hollywood Reporter he saw the letter and raised it internally.[^26][^30]

people.name: Edgar Wright
people.text: Organised the first letter after emailing Steven Spielberg, enlisting Guillermo del Toro and Rian Johnson to find more signers.[^30]

people.name: Kevin Bahr
people.text: Started “Keep FilmStruck Alive” on Change.org on the day of the announcement.[^24][^25]
